problem: Video/diffusion world models must stay consistent with long past histories, but transformers have quadratic attention cost and limited context, while recurrent/SSM models compress history and lose fidelity. Naive product-of-experts composition of memory models also over-sharpens and collapses consistency.
motivation: Imagined rollouts used for planning in navigation/RL are only useful if they stay consistent with previously seen places. Memory should be distributed across specialized components (like human STM/LTM) rather than crammed into a single architecture, and diffusion models allow inference-time composition of experts without retraining.
key_idea: Compose a short-term memory expert, a long-term memory expert (LoRA test-time-finetuned diffusion weights storing episodic history) and a spatial long-term memory expert via a product of contrastive experts (conditional^alpha x unconditional^(1-alpha)) at diffusion sampling time.
insight: The contrastive formulation is essential: without it, stacking experts barely helps or hurts (all experts LPIPS 0.192 without vs 0.097 with contrast), because it reweights modes without narrowing kernels as plain tempering does. LoRA test-time adaptation gives implicit regularization (full finetuning is worse at 50/150 frames: 0.221/0.188 vs 0.162/0.142 for rank 256) and LTM keeps improving up to 450-480 frames, so memory can scale without quadratic attention.
method: Product of Contrastive Experts (PoCE): each expert p_i is combined with its unconditional baseline as p_i^alpha_i * pbar_i^(1-alpha_i), alpha in [2,3]; at sampling it is a weighted sum of conditional and unconditional scores/noise predictions; KDE proposition shows it reweights mode weights without changing kernel shapes
Short-term memory (STM): a smaller DiT-S with sliding-window attention (chunk 20, two full-attention layers) attending 33 (10-100) recent frames; contrastive baseline is its unconditional model

Long-term memory (LTM): the base diffusion model with LoRA adapters (rank 8-256) finetuned at test time on 100-1000 past frames with the diffusion loss (2-3 steps per frame); contrastive baseline is the model without adaptation; continuously updated in streaming

Spatial LTM (SLTM): a DiT conditioned on spatial signals (absolute camera pose / position from an auxiliary encoder or SLAM/VGGT-style), also test-time trained; contrastive baseline drops the spatial prior
Base I2V/DiT prior p_theta conditioned on 1-3 recent frames, composed with the three experts in a single joint score
Online loop: memorize new clips into LoRA weights, sample with composite score, append ground truth or generated frames to memory

setting.backbone: DiT-B base with DiT-S STM, LoRA LTM, and SLTM DiT; pretrained DFoT model on RE10K; NWM (DiT-B STM) on RECON; UViT/UNet on DMLab/Memory Cards
setting.model_size: DiT-B base; STM/SLTM about 45% of base parameters; LoRA rank 8-256 (1%-25% params)
setting.training_data: Memory Maze (30k trajectories x 1k frames), RE10K, RECON (5k trajectories), DMLab-40K, Minecraft, Memory Cards (100k sequences); models trained 150k steps; LTM finetuned at test time on the episode history
setting.observation: monocular RGB video frames plus camera pose / relative or absolute position
setting.action_space: none for a policy (video world model with relative/absolute pose conditioning; for planning, NWM candidate trajectories scored by rollouts)
setting.simulator: Memory Maze, DMLab, Minecraft, Memory Cards (pygame); offline datasets RE10K and RECON
setting.privileged: ground-truth past frames appended as context in streaming evaluation; absolute poses for SLTM; goal image for planning

numbers_note: No standard embodied navigation benchmarks; these are world-model consistency and RECON planning metrics. Streaming Memory Maze results are only shown in a figure.
results: On Memory Maze CoME reaches LPIPS 0.097/SSIM 0.892/PSNR 23.07, beating the full-attention baseline (0.113/0.859/22.78) and STM+LTM (0.114) at much lower training cost. On RECON planning it lowers ATE/RPE to 0.96/0.28 versus NWM 1.13/0.35, and on RE10K recall LPIPS is 0.359 versus 0.405 for the base and 0.400-0.414 for history guidance.
limitations: Sensitive to quality and capacity of each expert; a weak expert can degrade the fused prediction
Test-time memorization adds about 2-4x compute overhead, plus extra forward passes per expert
Planning evaluation is limited to NWM on RECON with small gains, and there are no real-robot or standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmarks
